headline: Government's budget raises defence spending and cuts taxes
deck: Students living at home lose their state grant to help pay for it; talks with the other parties come next.
extended: The government presented its finance bill for 2027, the state's budget, on Friday. It would raise defence spending to 3.5 per cent of GDP by 2030 and set aside 10.1 billion kroner that year for tax cuts, among them scrapping the middle-bracket and top-top taxes and lowering corporate tax.

Unlike recent budgets, this one needs financing. Students living at home lose SU, the state study grant; fewer people will qualify for the seniorpension for worn-out workers; cruise ships face a levy; and state administration is to be cut.

'The Danish economy is in top form,' said Peter Hummelgaard, the finance minister. Pia Olsen Dyhr, the economy minister, called the grant cut 'a compromise'. Her party, SF, a left-wing party, has defended the grant.

The government must now find a majority in the Folketing, Denmark's parliament, and holds back 500 million kroner a year for other parties' wishes. Enhedslisten, a far-left party, and Alternativet, a green party, are expected to join the deal, and criticism of the grant cut has already come from them.
